# New generations learn differently; the challenge is to inspire them to love learning.

**This Wednesday, March 19, Apex took place, a space where various inspiring experiential learning initiatives, driven by the different schools and departments of EAFIT University, were presented in the Student Plaza by professors, administrative staff, and students.**

**The event was part of the fifth edition of Acción EAFIT, a week dedicated to experiential learning, with a special focus on methodologies based on games and simulations. Through training activities, demonstrations, and mentoring sessions, the university community has connected with the institutional educational model.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [EAFIT is in the News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/eafit-es-noticia)
- New generations learn differently; the challenge is to inspire them to love learning.

![Image: New generations learn differently; the challenge is to inspire them to love learning.](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/c46cbb68-68a9-4bea-b936-20cd9937fb44/web/accion-eafit-apex.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=Mn37ALu3)

The activities of Acción EAFIT will take place until this Thursday, March 20, with workshops, mentoring and networking spaces.

At the beginning of the corridor, Jenga pieces move in time with challenging questions. Further on, a giant die rolls, linking participants to a digital experience about the Institutional Self-Assessment Report. At another table, cards are revealed, one by one, to discuss legal concepts, while the more inquisitive explore worlds with augmented reality glasses.

All these experiences came to life this Wednesday, March 19, at Apex: _A Showcase of Inspiring Experiential Learning Initiatives_ , a space where games and simulations took center stage in a day that reaffirmed that, at EAFIT, learning is different. The event was held as part of the fifth edition of Acción EAFIT, a week in which the university community has gathered around a diverse program focused on the institution's educational model.

Teachers and students from the five Schools, administrative staff from the University and guests from Hontanares College shared how experiential learning is experienced inside and outside the classroom.

One example of this is _Innverso_ , an initiative led by Jorge Hernán Mesa Cano, a professor at the EAFIT School of Management. “We set out to find an industry with a problem and develop games as an alternative. We selected the coffee industry, which faces a challenge in generational succession. From there, we challenged ourselves to attract young people to the world of coffee, and the same thing happens in universities: new generations learn differently, the challenge is to inspire them to love learning,” says the professor.

_Innverso_ is currently a _spin-off company_ with seven games designed to strengthen the ability to imagine, innovate, and undertake entrepreneurial ventures. This initiative originated within the Entrepreneurship and Innovation Research Group and has been integrated into the Imagination and Creativity course, part of the Institutional Training Core, as an effective strategy for developing various skills in students.

The impact of these games has led to the creation of the Games Club, a space where students from various disciplines explore playful learning. Jerónimo Gil Giraldo, a Mathematical Engineering student and club member, highlights how these activities improve concentration and learning, encouraging participants to actively engage in class. “I think that nowadays attention is easily lost. When you play, you have something tangible in your hands, which helps you focus more. Plus, you learn in different, more engaging ways.”

As part of the institutional accreditation process, EAFIT has implemented an innovative gamification strategy, designed by the School of Arts and Humanities. Through its ecosystem of laboratories, Ecolabs, and the undergraduate program in Interactive Design, a challenge game was created based on a narrative featuring the character Lardi. Its purpose is to strengthen the understanding of the self-evaluation results and foster a sense of belonging to the University.

“It works like a ‘path of life,’ where Lardi, based on a squirrel (an emblematic character of the University), accompanies participants through the accreditation process. As they progress, they must answer questions and, depending on their performance, receive cards with scores. At the end of the journey, depending on the number of points obtained, they can take home a _souvenir_ ,” explains Paula Colorado Chávez, a professor at the School of Arts and Humanities.

The Luis Echavarría Villegas Cultural Center and Library also joined Apex with three activities designed to promote game-based learning. One of these was a virtual tour of its facilities using augmented reality glasses, in which participants faced challenges to explore and learn more about the available resources.

In addition, Luis Fernando Ramírez Quintero, a member of the information and digital literacy training team, highlighted that the library has specialized bibliographic material on gamification, available in both physical and digital formats. These resources can be requested on the second floor of the library or via email [at formacion@eafit.edu.co.](mailto:formacion@eafit.edu.co)

Otra iniciativa destacada en Apex fue Kratos, un grupo estudiantil de EAFIT que resuelve desafíos tecnológicos y de ingeniería a través de proyectos innovadores. María Gabriela Zabala Barrios, estudiante de quinto semestre de Ingeniería Mecánica y miembro del grupo desde hace dos años, explica que Kratos trabaja en retos propuestos tanto por empresas como por los mismos estudiantes.

“Hemos desarrollado varios proyectos. Por ejemplo, Postobón, uno de nuestros patrocinadores, nos presentó un reto en el que sus operarios debían cargar manualmente cajas con botellas. Nosotros diseñamos un vehículo que facilita su movilidad y reduce la carga laboral”, señala.

Además de proyectos aplicados a la industria, Kratos participa en competencias como la de Vehículos de Tracción Humana (VTH), donde los estudiantes diseñan, manufacturan y promueven sus creaciones. Aunque su base es la ingeniería, el grupo está abierto a estudiantes de todas las áreas, reconociendo el valor de la interdisciplinariedad en la resolución de problemas.

###### Aprender jugando, simulando y haciendo

El aprendizaje experiencial es un pilar fundamental en el modelo educativo de la Universidad, ya que se adapta a las nuevas generaciones y a sus formas de adquirir conocimiento. Para el profesor Jorge Hernán, esta metodología es clave porque "el aprendizaje hoy es para toda la vida, y si lo hacemos a través de juegos es mucho mejor. Motiva a los estudiantes y les ofrece herramientas para desarrollar habilidades significativas y duraderas".

Desde la perspectiva docente, esta transformación responde a la necesidad constante de evolución en la educación. La profesora Paula destaca que "la educación siempre está en constante cambio, y la didáctica debe adaptarse a las necesidades del entorno. Nuestros estudiantes cada vez demandan más y, como profesores, también exigimos más recursos y nuevas formas de enseñanza, no solo para hacernos entender, sino para generar interacciones más directas y circulares".

Los estudiantes también reconocen el valor de estas metodologías, pues les permiten aplicar el conocimiento en contextos reales. María Gabriela resalta que "lo que aprendo, tanto de modelaciones como de soldadura, lo puedo aplicar en Kratos de una manera mucho más práctica". Esto no solo mejora su preparación profesional, sino que también fortalece su confianza al enfrentarse a desafíos reales antes de ingresar al mundo laboral. Así, el aprendizaje experiencial no solo transforma la manera de enseñar, sino que prepara a los estudiantes para un futuro en el que la teoría y la práctica van de la mano.
